data.title: Nebius, CoreWeave, and IREN Stocks Rebound After Heavy Losses — Can the Rally Last?
data.description:
After weeks of heavy selling, neocloud stocks are showing signs of recovery, with Nebius (NASDAQ:NBIS), CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), and IREN (NASDAQ:IREN) climbing around 5% in Thursday's premarket session. The rebound comes as excitement surrounding Anthropic's highly anticipated Nasdaq debut lifts investor sentiment toward companies providing computing capacity for artificial intelligence applications.

Anthropic's record-breaking IPO, priced at $83 per share and valuing the ChatGPT rival at $1.5 trillion, has reinforced expectations that demand for advanced infrastructure will continue growing. The developer's extensive computing investments could benefit specialized cloud providers, although concerns about excessive spending and financing requirements have weighed heavily on their valuations.

With these three stocks trading well below previous highs, Wall Street's forecasts suggest investors may have reasons to reconsider their prospects.

Nebius Is Betting Billions on AI — Wall Street Sees a Big Payoff

For Nebius, attracting customers is hardly the problem. The AI infrastructure provider has accumulated billions in contracted commitments, yet its stock has struggled as investors grow concerned about the cost of meeting that demand. Third-quarter revenue surged 571% year-over-year to $980.8 million, while remaining performance obligations reached $38.7 billion, illustrating just how much future revenue is riding on the company's expansion plans.

However, investors were disappointed when Nebius lowered its 2026 revenue forecast to between $3 billion and $3.2 billion, citing delays in securing third-party data-center capacity. The company also raised its annual spending outlook to $27 billion, with another $40 billion to $45 billion expected in 2027. These figures have raised concerns about the financial commitments required to sustain such rapid expansion.

Despite these challenges, Nebius expects revenue to reach between $12 billion and $13 billion next year, with customer prepayments and asset-backed financing expected to cover most planned investments. The company also anticipates reaching pretax break-even by the end of 2027, although execution risks remain.

Wall Street appears willing to look beyond these near-term obstacles, with NBIS receiving a Moderate Buy consensus rating supported by 9 Buys, 2 Holds, and one Sell. Its average 12-month price target stands at $260.90, implying ~144% upside from Wednesday's closing price. (See NBIS stock forecast)

CoreWeave's $132.5 Billion Backlog Isn't Enough to Silence the Skeptics

CoreWeave has also experienced a turbulent November, as investors weigh its expanding operations against the mounting costs of building data centers. The company's third-quarter results offered some reassurance, with revenue reaching $3.66 billion, compared with $1.37 billion a year earlier. Its contracted backlog also climbed to $132.5 billion, providing greater visibility into future customer demand.

The cloud provider raised its full-year sales forecast to between $13 billion and $13.3 billion, while anticipating about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the following three months. These developments helped ease concerns about financing, although a quarterly net loss of $709 million and interest expenses totaling $846 million remain troubling.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's leadership turmoil and political concerns surrounding data-center construction have added to the uncertainty facing CoreWeave. Nevertheless, Anthropic's IPO offers another reminder of the computing requirements facing AI developers, with this infrastructure specialist already counting the company among its customers.

Wall Street remains bullish on CRWV stock, awarding it a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 20 Buys, 6 Holds, and 3 Sells. The average 12-month price target of $104.70 suggests ~119% upside from Wednesday's closing price. (See CRWV stock forecast)

IREN Has Lost Investors' Confidence, but Wall Street Sees 270% Upside

IREN's recent stock performance suggests investors are looking beyond impressive growth figures and focusing on what comes next. The company's expansion into AI cloud services has delivered rapid revenue gains, but financing concerns have taken a toll on its valuation. Computing revenue climbed 182% sequentially to $200 million in the latest quarter, helping total sales reach $228 million, even as doubts about the cost of future expansion continued to weigh on sentiment.

The company also reported a $20.3 billion backlog and confirmed that its target of more than $4 billion in contracted annual recurring revenue remains funded. However, customer-requested modifications and supplier delays have pushed the expected delivery of associated capacity into early 2027, creating another source of uncertainty.

Financing remains a central concern, with IREN disclosing that about $6 billion of its remaining planned fiscal 2027 capital expenditures would require additional funding sources. Potential solutions include GPU-backed loans, customer prepayments, and other arrangements, while a quarterly net loss of $263 million illustrates the financial challenges accompanying expansion.

Despite these concerns, analysts remain positive about IREN's longer-term prospects, awarding the stock a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on eight Buys and three Holds, with no Sell recommendations. Its average price target of $56.50 suggests 270% upside from the Wednesday's closing price. (See IREN stock forecast)

Can the Neocloud Rally Last?

Wall Street's forecasts suggest that analysts see strong recovery potential in all three stocks, with IREN leading on projected upside, followed by Nebius and CoreWeave. Nevertheless, Thursday's rebound appears driven largely by improving sentiment surrounding Anthropic's IPO rather than any resolution of the financial challenges facing these companies.

For the recovery to develop into a sustained rally, investors will likely need evidence that AI computing demand continues translating into revenue, while expansion costs and borrowing requirements remain manageable. Until then, the gap between current share prices and analysts' targets offers encouragement, but it does not guarantee that the recent volatility has ended.
data.author: Ben Yoffe

data.title: DELL, MRVL, ADI: 3 AI Stocks to Buy Ahead of Next Week's Earnings, According to Analysts
data.description:
AI hardware and chip stocks Dell Technologies (DELL), Analog Devices (ADI), and Marvell Technology (MRVL) will report their quarterly results next week. Analog Devices and Dell are both slated to report on Tuesday, November 24, followed by Marvell on Thursday, November 26.

The three companies serve different parts of the tech sector. Dell makes AI servers, Analog Devices supplies chips, and Marvell makes custom chips for data centers. According to TipRanks data, analysts see the most upside in Marvell at 122.36%. Dell follows at 88.21%, while Analog Devices offers 26.55%.

Here is the breakdown of all three stocks and what Wall Street expects from them.

Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL)

Dell Technologies provides IT systems for businesses, including AI servers, storage, and PCs. Demand for AI servers has helped build its backlog to $95 billion.

Dell is scheduled to report its fiscal Q3 2027 results after the market closes on November 24. Wall Street expects adjusted earnings of $6.60 per share, up sharply from $2.59 in the year-ago quarter. Revenue is projected to jump roughly 82% year-over-year to $49.25 billion.

According to TipRanks, DELL stock has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 14 Buys and seven Holds assigned over the past three months. At $589.32, the average analyst price target implies 88.21% upside from current levels.

Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI)

Analog Devices makes chips that process real-world signals. Its products are used in factories, cars, communications systems, and data centers.

The company will report its fiscal Q4 2026 results before the market opens on November 24. Analysts expect Analog Devices to post earnings of $3.89 per share, up from $2.26 a year earlier. Meanwhile, quarterly revenue is projected to reach $4.32 billion.

On TipRanks, ADI carries a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 16 Buys and one Hold. Its average 12-month price target of $483.40 implies 26.55% upside potential.

Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL)

Marvell Technology makes chips that help data centers handle AI workloads. Its products support AI computing and high-speed data links.

Marvell is estimated to announce its fiscal Q3 2027 results on November 26. Wall Street forecasts MRVL to report adjusted earnings of $1.10 per share, representing a 44.7% increase from $0.76 per share in the same period last year. Revenue is expected to surge 52.2% year-over-year to $3.15 billion.

 Marvell currently holds a Strong Buy consensus rating on TipRanks, based on 24 Buys and five Holds issued in the last three months. Marvell's average analyst price target of $323.63 points to 122.36% upside from current levels.

data.title: U.S. Stock Futures Gain from Optimism Around Anthropic's IPO
data.description:
U.S. stock futures rose Thursday morning as investors focused on Claude AI maker Anthropic's (ANT) Nasdaq debut. The AI company priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its initial $70-$78 target range. Anthropic also upsized its offering, selling 980 million shares to raise $81.3 billion. It surpassed SpaceX's (SPCX) $75 billion June offering, making it the largest IPO on record.

Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 2.21%, 1.26%, and 0.66%, respectively, as of 8:22 a.m. EST on November 19.

Meanwhile, oil prices rose on Thursday morning after falling in the previous session. Rising global oil supply and higher U.S. interest rates are limiting gains, while persistent geopolitical risks in the Middle East are supporting higher prices. At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.89% to $92.77 per barrel, while WTI crude futures rose 1.03% to $84.12 per barrel.

During Wednesday's regular trading session, the three major U.S. indexes closed mixed. The Dow Jones and the S&P 500 fell 1.11% and 0.23%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.42%.

In premarket trading, Walmart (WMT) stock fell despite the big-box retailer raising its full-year outlook, driven by strength in e-commerce sales. In contrast, Palo Alto (PANW) shares jumped after the cybersecurity company reported solid Q1 FY27 results and announced the $4.5 billion acquisition of Applied Compute.

Additionally, Intel (INTC) shares rose as CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the chipmaker has signed its first external customer for its 18A chips, CNBC reported. Pushkar Ranade, Intel's technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer signed up for Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June.

Shares of neocloud companies and chip and AI-related stocks also advanced in premarket trading as Anthropic's IPO lifted investor sentiment. However, Alibaba's (BABA) U.S.-listed shares fell as the Chinese e-commerce and cloud company missed earnings estimates. The company's huge AI spending also weighed on the stock.

data.title: 3 Construction Stocks with More Than 70% Upside and 'Strong Buy' Ratings, According to Analysts
data.description:
Dycom Industries (DY), Sterling Infrastructure (STRL), and MasTec (MTZ) are three infrastructure construction companies with more than 70% upside and 'Strong Buy' ratings, according to analysts. These companies provide construction and maintenance services across telecommunications, transportation, utilities, and energy projects.

While construction stocks naturally go through ups and downs with the broader economy, steady spending on roads, power grids, data centers, and industrial sites gives these businesses plenty of room to grow over the long haul. Using the TipRanks Stock Screener tool, we found that these three stocks stand out in the sector because of their high analyst upside and consensus. Let us take a closer look at each company.

1. Dycom Industries (DY) — Dycom provides specialty contracting services for telecommunications, digital infrastructure, and utility projects in the United States. Its portfolio includes fiber-optic networks, wireless infrastructure, and utility construction. The company is scheduled to report Q3 2027 earnings on November 24, 2026. Ahead of earnings, analysts estimate net sales of $1.95 billion and earnings per share (EPS) of $4.59. Year-to-date, the stock is down about 33%.

On Wall Street, Dycom has a Strong Buy rating, with 10 of the 11 analysts covering the stock rating it a Buy. The average DY stock price target of $545.50 implies about 142% upside from the last price of $225.78. KeyBanc recently reiterated its Buy rating on Dycom with a target price of $429. TipRanks assigns Dycom a Smart Score of 7.

2. Sterling Infrastructure (STRL) — Sterling Infrastructure divides its operations across three core areas: transportation, e-infrastructure, and building solutions. Rather than focusing on a single niche, its projects range from roads, bridges, airports, and water systems to concrete foundations and site development for data centers. The company reported a 127% year-over-year revenue increase in its Q3 2026 results released last month. EPS also reached a record $7.58, up 118% year-over-year. For the full year, the company raised its revenue guidance to $4.63 billion to $4.73 billion.

TipRanks forecast shows a Strong Buy consensus for Sterling, with all seven analysts rating the stock a Buy. The average price target of $645 suggests about 133% upside from current price levels. However, some analysts have lowered their price targets for the company after the earnings report. Cantor Fitzgerald cut its price target on Sterling Infrastructure to $565 from $742 while maintaining an Overweight rating, noting that growth is limited by execution capacity rather than demand despite management reaffirming its 20% to 30% organic profit growth outlook. Sterling has a TipRanks Smart Score of 7.

3. MasTec (MTZ) — MasTec works with utility, energy, and telecom clients to build and maintain essential infrastructure across North America. That work spans electrical transmission grids, oil and gas pipelines, renewable power facilities, and broadband and wireless networks. The infrastructure firm reported third-quarter earnings last month and beat analyst estimates for both revenue and EPS. Revenue rose about 30% year-over-year to $5.2 billion, while EPS increased 19.3% year-over-year to $2.96 from $2.48. Management expects 2026 full-year cash flow from operations to exceed $1 billion.

MTZ has been covered by 17 analysts over the last three months. 16 analysts rate it a Buy, while one analyst rates it a Hold. The average MTZ stock price target of $305.75 represents a 74.82% upside. Morgan Stanley (MS) initiated coverage on MasTec with an Equal Weight rating and a $220 price target, noting that while the company has multiple earnings drivers, uncertainty around communications demand and execution makes it a "show me" story. The company has a Smart Score of 5 on TipRanks.

data.title: Anthropic Pays Wall Street Banks $550 Million on Record $107.3 Billion IPO
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) agreed to pay $550 million to the Wall Street banks working on its $107.3 billion initial public offering, a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing shows. This payout tops the $500 million banks earned on SpaceX's (SPCX) $86.2 billion listing in June, the previous record holder for the largest IPO ever.

The Claude chatbot maker is paying underwriters nearly 68 basis points, or about 0.68% of the IPO proceeds, the SEC filing shows. This rate sits roughly in line with the 0.58% fee banks shared on SpaceX's deal.

Anthropic priced its shares at $83 ahead of Thursday's Nasdaq debut. Goldman Sachs (GS) edged up and Morgan Stanley (MS) gained too on Thursday, while SpaceX (SPCX) also ticked up.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley Lead 22-Bank Group

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley took the top roles on Anthropic's IPO, matching the lead spots they held on SpaceX.

Another 20 banks worked on the offering and will split a share of the total raised, the SEC filing shows. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley each collected $100 million from SpaceX's $500 million fee pool in June, Bloomberg previously reported.

 Anthropic Gets to Skip Bank Fees on Extra IPO Shares

Anthropic also copied an unusual cost-saving move from SpaceX's listing. Both companies chose to pay $0 in bank fees on the over-allotment shares, also known as a greenshoe, the SEC filing shows.

Anthropic gave underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to 147 million extra Class A shares. Banks can use those extra shares to support the stock if the price drops in early trading.

Mega-IPOs Lift Bank Equity Revenue

Average IPOs raise less than $1 billion and typically pay investment banks 4% to 7% of the deal size. Fee rates fall a lot on large listings, a trade-off banks accept to climb higher on industry league table.

SpaceX's debut helped Wall Street's biggest banks bring in their highest second-quarter revenue from equity offerings since 2021, data compiled by Bloomberg shows. Goldman Sachs ranked first in those league tables for the quarter ended September 30.

Anthropic and its seven co-founders raised $107.3 billion across the upsized IPO and a private share sale alongside it. Thursday's debut marks the first public listing by a company focused mainly on building advanced AI models.

What Is the Forecast for ANT Stock?

Four Wall Street analysts now cover ANT stock with Buy ratings, giving it a Strong Buy rating overall. The average 12-month ANT stock price target sits at $133.75.

Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes set the top target at $155, while Needham analyst Scott Berg set a $150 target. Citizens JMP analyst Patrick Walravens put his target at $125, and New Street Research analyst Pierre Ferragu set the low target at $105.

From the $83 IPO price, the average target points to about 61.1% upside. Individual targets point to gains between 26.5% and 86.7%.
data.author: Annika Masrani

data.title: Marvell Stock Price Forecast: Options Traders Expect a Large Move in MRVL Stock After Q3 Earnings
data.description:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) will announce its fiscal third-quarter earnings after the market closes on Thursday, November 26. According to TipRanks' Options Trading Tool, options traders expect a massive 11.25% move in either direction in MRVL stock in reaction to the semiconductor company's Q3 FY27 earnings. The options-implied move measures the expected size of the price change, not whether the stock will rise or fall.

Notably, Marvell stock has seen mixed reactions following earnings. Over the last four reports, shares fell 10.28% and gained 3.08%, 18.35%, and 7.87% the next day. These moves reflect an average absolute price change of 9.90%.

MRVL Stock Price Performance

Marvell Technology stock trended higher in Thursday's premarket trading after falling 2.15% to close at $145.54 on Wednesday. The premarket rebound comes as AI infrastructure sentiment gets a lift ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut following its $83 IPO pricing. Investors are also watching demand for data center connectivity and AI memory. Year-to-date, the stock has gained over 71%.

Recent Events Ahead of the Report

  • Recent developments for Marvell include its November 16 collaboration with Penguin Solutions (PENG). The two companies will work on CXL-based memory expansion and photonic optical interconnect technology for large-scale AI data centers.
  • Marvell is also preparing to acquire Lumentum (LITE) under a $115 billion all-stock deal announced on November 2. The deal aims to expand its AI connectivity business, but concerns about share dilution have weighed on the stock.

Analysts' Take on MRVL Stock

Following the Lumentum deal, TD Cowen analyst Sean O'Loughlin downgraded Marvell to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $175 from $350. O'Loughlin expects the Lumentum deal to dilute earnings per share by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2028. He also worries the deal may come near the peak of an optical market cycle. O'Loughlin said his downgrade reflects concerns about the deal's structure and timing, rather than Lumentum's business.

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya also lowered its rating to Neutral from Buy and cut its price target to $225 from $400. Arya cited potential share dilution and a long regulatory process. He also noted that the deal could face customer conflicts.

Is MRVL Stock a Buy Now?

Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Marvell Technology stock, with 24 Buys and five Holds. The average MRVL stock price target of $323.63 indicates 122% upside potential.

data.title: Why Micron, Sandisk, and Intel Stocks Are Rallying Today, Nov. 19 — and What Wall Street Sees Next
data.description:
Chip stocks are staging a comeback in Thursday's premarket session, with Micron (NASDAQ:MU), SanDisk (NASDAQ:SNDK), and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) all gaining between 4% and 5%. The rebound follows weeks of heavy selling, as enthusiasm surrounding Anthropic's highly anticipated Nasdaq debut lifts sentiment toward tech companies that could benefit from the AI developer's future infrastructure investments.

Anthropic's IPO will provide the ChatGPT rival with additional capital for computing infrastructure, potentially increasing demand for advanced processors, memory chips, and data-center storage. Meanwhile, Intel has another reason to rally following encouraging news regarding its manufacturing operations.

Micron's AI Opportunity Remains Intact Despite Mounting Risks

Micron has endured a turbulent month, with the scandal surrounding Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, concerns about excessive AI spending, and the Democrats' sweeping midterm victories weighing on semiconductor stocks. The election results have raised fears of tighter restrictions on data-center construction, potentially slowing demand for advanced memory chips. Despite these challenges, expectations for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) remain encouraging, supported by continued investment in AI infrastructure.

Nvidia's latest earnings also offered another reason to reconsider Micron's prospects. The chip giant disclosed that its supply commitments had climbed from $279 billion to $390 billion, with much of that increase related to multiyear procurement agreements. For Micron, which provides HBM components used in AI accelerators, these obligations suggest customer requirements could remain elevated.

There have also been encouraging developments regarding memory-chip pricing, with expectations of continued industry strength supporting Micron's longer-term prospects. However, legal uncertainty remains after a federal judge allowed a proposed DRAM price-fixing lawsuit involving Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron to proceed. While the allegations remain unproven, the case introduces another potential risk for investors evaluating future returns.

Despite the recent turbulence, Wall Street remains extremely bullish on Micron's longer-term prospects. MU stock boasts a Strong Buy consensus rating, supported by 28 Buys and just one Hold assigned during the past three months. The average 12-month price target of $1,624.42 suggests an upside potential of 130% from Wednesday's closing price.

SanDisk's Stock Split Arrives at a Critical Moment

SanDisk has also experienced heavy selling in recent weeks, although its latest financial results suggest underlying demand for storage products remains healthy. The company continues benefiting from data-center expansion, where customers require greater capacity to support AI applications.

In late October, the manufacturer reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.03 billion, representing a 23% increase from the preceding period. Its non-GAAP gross margin reached 85.1%, while executives projected second-quarter sales between $12.2 billion and $12.6 billion, reflecting expectations for continued customer spending.

However, concerns about a possible NAND flash memory glut have complicated the outlook for storage manufacturers. GF Securities recently warned about potential oversupply and weaker pricing, contributing to another selloff throughout the sector. SanDisk also faces longer-term competition from Chinese producers seeking greater participation in the global market.

Meanwhile, investors are preparing for the company's eight-for-one stock split, with adjusted trading scheduled to begin on November 20. Although this corporate action leaves its underlying valuation unchanged, smaller individual share prices could make ownership more accessible to retail participants.

Wall Street appears convinced that SanDisk's recent weakness has created an attractive buying opportunity, with analysts projecting 174% upside potential based on the average 12-month price target of $2,130.83. SNDK has earned a Strong Buy consensus rating, supported by 11 Buys and 3 Holds. (See SNDK stock forecast)

Intel Lands a Customer That Could Change Its Future

Intel's Thursday rally has an additional catalyst beyond the broader semiconductor recovery, following an announcement that could strengthen its long-running manufacturing turnaround.

CEO Lip-Bu Tan revealed Wednesday that the company had signed what he described as its first external customer for advanced 18A technology. The unnamed client selected Intel's 18A-P process, marking an important commercial milestone for its foundry operations.

The chipmaker also named Microsoft as the first publicly disclosed customer for its EMIB advanced packaging technology, providing another encouraging development. Their expanded relationship includes multiyear Xeon supply-capacity commitments, offering Intel another opportunity to demonstrate its competitiveness within data centers.

These announcements follow a challenging October, when disappointing fourth-quarter revenue guidance raised concerns about weakening PC demand and supply-chain constraints. Shares have lost about 39% over the past month, leaving investors eager for evidence that the turnaround strategy is delivering results.

Unlike Micron and SanDisk, Intel has yet to convince most Wall Street analysts that its recovery deserves an outright bullish recommendation. INTC stock holds a Hold consensus rating, based on 7 Buys, 25 Holds, and one Sell assigned during the past three months. Nevertheless, the average 12-month price target of $90.93 suggests a potential upside of 66% from Wednesday's closing price. (See INTC stock forecast)
data.author: Ben Yoffe

The company is also raising an additional $26 billion through a private placement.

Meanwhile, oil prices edged higher on Thursday after falling in the previous session. Concerns about rising global oil supply and higher U.S. interest rates limited gains, while renewed geopolitical risks in the Middle East supported prices. Reports of possible further U.S. action against Iran and attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz also kept supply concerns in focus.

At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.76% to $92.65 per barrel, while WTI crude futures rose 0.65% to $83.80 per barrel.

Looking ahead, investors will also watch data on weekly jobless claims for further clues about the strength of the U.S. labor market. On the earnings front, results from Walmart (WMT), Alibaba (BABA), and Gap (GAP) are scheduled for release today. 

Global Markets

European markets traded mixed on Thursday, while Asia-Pacific markets closed mostly lower. Investors remained cautious ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, as concerns about AI valuations and the outlook for U.S. interest rates continued to weigh on sentiment.

Investors also kept an eye on the trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The talks could focus on nuclear arms control, the Ukraine war, and global security. Any progress could ease geopolitical tensions and improve investor sentiment.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index dropped 1.95%. In China, the Shanghai Composite fell 0.28%, and the Shenzhen Component was down 1.20%. The Nikkei 225 added 0.71% and the Topix declined 0.04%.

data.title: Cathie Wood Loads Up on AI and Biotech Stocks, Cuts One EV Holding
data.description:
On Wednesday, Cathie Wood's ARK Invest bought shares of AI and biotech companies while cutting its stake in one electric vehicle (EV) maker. According to the firm's daily fund disclosures, ARK bought shares of Kodiak AI (KDK), Twist Bioscience (TWST), Scribe Therapeutics (SCTX), and GeneDx Holdings (WGS), while selling shares of BYD (BYDDY).

On the sell side, ARK Invest sold 59,498 shares of BYD (BYDDY) through its Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ). The sale was worth about $478,958. This follows several sales over the past week, showing that ARK has continued to reduce its BYD holdings.

Wood Adds Kodiak AI Stock

ARK Invest bought 506,083 shares of Kodiak AI through its ARKQ. The purchase was worth about $551,630. ARK has previously accumulated KDK shares several times in 2026, including in April, May, and October.

Kodiak AI develops autonomous driving technology for commercial trucks and defense. In Q3 2026, the company reported revenue of $3 million, up 286% year-over-year. It posted a GAAP operating loss of $50.4 million. The figures highlight the early-stage nature of the business and the risks tied to its long-term growth plans. KDK stock is down 90% year-to-date.

Cathie Wood continues to add AI stocks focused on real-world uses. Through ARKQ, her team is betting on Kodiak's self-driving truck technology and its potential to change freight transport. However, ARK's purchases are long-term bets, and the company still has a long way to go before autonomous trucking becomes widely used.

Wood Buys More Biotech Shares

ARK Invest also bought shares of other biotech companies. Through its ARK Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG), the fund purchased 2,835 shares of Twist Bioscience, worth about $317,520. The same ETF added 11,539 shares of Scribe Therapeutics, valued at around $181,970. This follows several recent purchases of the gene-editing company.

Separately, ARK Invest bought 4,319 shares of GeneDx Holdings through its ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK). The purchase was worth about $204,245.

Kodiak AI Stock Signals Strong Upside Ahead

According to TipRanks' Stock Comparison Tool, KDK and WGS stocks have Strong Buy ratings. KDK's average price target of $8.43 implies 695% upside, while WGS's average target of $83.80 points to a potential gain of 61%.

Twist Bioscience and Scribe Therapeutics stocks have Moderate Buy ratings with potential upside of 13% and 327%, respectively.

data.title: Anthropic Gray Market Signals 24% Jump After Record $107.3 Billion IPO Beats SpaceX
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) shares pointed up to 24% higher in gray market trading before their Thursday debut in New York, Bloomberg reported. The early jump follows an upsized $107.3 billion IPO and private sale that beat SpaceX (SPCX) as the largest first-time share sale ever.

The stock starts trading today on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after U.S. markets open at 9:30 a.m. ET.

The Claude chatbot maker priced its stock at $83 for a $1.5 trillion value. Derivatives at IG International pointed to a 24% gain early Thursday. Crypto futures on Hyperliquid also traded near $102, or 20% above the IPO price, on over $140 million in daily volume.

Nvidia and Google Join Record $107.3 Billion Deal

Anthropic and its seven co-founders raised $107.3 billion in total, including a $26 billion private placement from backers such as Nvidia (NVDA), Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google, and AMD (AMD). Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) led the IPO with 20 other banks, regulatory filings show.

Wall Street is watching the debut after Nvidia shares fell this month following Jensen Huang's exit and AI spending worries. U.S. IPOs have dropped a weighted average of 4% this year, Bloomberg data shows. Still, Nasdaq 100 futures rose 1.8% early Thursday, and Polymarket traders put 46% odds on Anthropic hitting $1.75 trillion by year-end.

"With a well-priced IPO, you always need to leave a little upside," Jacques-Aurélien Marcireau, CEO of Stilgar AM, told Bloomberg.

Anthropic Has Grown Its Revenue Run Rate to $81 Billion

More companies have been paying to use Anthropic's tools and this is what has made ANT stock an easier sell to investors. Anthropic's annual revenue run rate hit $81 billion on October 31, up $10 billion in a month, regulatory filings show. Over 11,900 customers now bring in at least $100,000 a year, up from about 1,500 in 2025.

Software developers widely use its Claude Code tool, including NASA engineers, the filings show. Anthropic is also pushing into law and healthcare, and Goldman Sachs analysts think its sales could reach about $685 billion by 2030.

Moreover, Bloomberg Intelligence estimates sales could reach $200 billion by 2028 even after 20% price cuts on some models.

Anthropic Is Facing $901 Billion in Computing Bills

Staying ahead in AI tends to come with large bills. Anthropic's spending commitments hit nearly $901 billion, mostly for chips and computing power, filings show. About $71 billion is due in the year through September 2027.

Investors should also see whether cheaper open-weight models from Chinese rivals squeeze margins. Anthropic has promised to keep Claude ad-free, and its Long-Term Benefit Trust holds power to pick or remove most board members.

"Once advertising becomes part of a company's revenue targets, the pressure to optimize for engagement tends to grow," the co-founders wrote in an investor letter in the filings. "We have chosen not to introduce that pressure into Claude."

What Is the Forecast for ANT Stock?

Four Wall Street analysts now cover ANT stock with Buy ratings, giving it a Strong Buy rating overall. The average 12-month ANT stock price target sits at $133.75.

Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes set the top target at $155, while Needham analyst Scott Berg set a $150 target. Citizens JMP analyst Patrick Walravens put his target at $125, and New Street Research analyst Pierre Ferragu set the low target at $105.

From the $83 IPO price, the average target points to about 61.1% upside. Individual targets point to gains between 26.5% and 86.7%.
